name: quantum-free-journals
description: Bundled demo set over the single-page document 'Free journals with 0 APC charges'. Ingest that PDF as a public document before running; point --cases at your own file for a different corpus.

cases.question: Which journal offers a no-questions-asked fee waiver, and what must an author do to get it?
cases.expected_output: Quantum (quantum-journal.org) offers a no-questions-asked waiver. During submission the author ticks a box saying 'I cannot pay the fee'; no proof is required and the waiver is granted automatically.

cases.question: Is SciPost Physics free to publish in, and how is it funded?
cases.expected_output: Yes. SciPost Physics charges 0 APC. It is strictly Diamond Open Access, funded by a consortium of universities.

cases.question: Which journal is recommended for quantum machine learning papers?
cases.expected_output: The Journal of Machine Learning Research (JMLR): a Q1, fully free journal that accepts high-quality theoretical quantum machine learning papers.

cases.question: What topics is Logical Methods in Computer Science (LMCS) suited for?
cases.expected_output: LMCS is a Q2, 0-APC theoretical computer science venue suited to quantum logic, quantum programming languages, and quantum semantics. It is run by the community on the Episciences platform.

cases.question: Which listed journal is best for quantum algorithms, complexity theory, and cryptography?
cases.expected_output: Theory of Computing: a Q2/Q3, free Diamond Open Access journal focused on strictly theoretical topics such as quantum algorithms, complexity theory, and cryptography.

cases.question: What is SciPost Physics Core?
cases.expected_output: SciPost Physics Core is a Q2 sister journal of SciPost Physics, for papers that are scientifically rigorous but less groundbreaking than those in the main journal.

cases.question: Which journals in the list are ranked Q1?
cases.expected_output: Three journals are Q1: Quantum, SciPost Physics, and the Journal of Machine Learning Research (JMLR).

cases.question: What is the official fee for the Quantum journal, and how can it be waived?
cases.expected_output: Quantum officially charges about 600 euros. Authors can get a no-questions-asked waiver by ticking the 'I cannot pay the fee' box; no proof is required.

cases.question: Which venue is run by the community on the Episciences platform?
What does SciPost Physics focus on?
cases.expected_output: High-quality physics research including quantum information, many-body quantum physics, and experimental quantum tech.
